title: Concurrency, Offline Replay & Data Integrity Stress Test

scenarios.name: Concurrent trip creation
scenarios.findings: Executed 5 simultaneous dispatchTrip requests. All trips received unique, sequential server-authoritative numbers (format Q-PRJ-0095-TRP-XXXXX) without collisions or sequence skipping.

scenarios.name: Idempotency
scenarios.findings: Replayed the same operationId across the Outbox sync pipeline. The second execution hit the server-authoritative syncOperationRepository idempotency check, returning an Idempotency Hit ACK without creating a duplicate trip or mutating state.

scenarios.name: Offline trip creation
scenarios.findings: Created trip in local Outbox with PENDING status. Upon online sync reconnection, operation was processed, server-authoritative trip identity was assigned, and local state transitioned to SYNCED exactly once.

scenarios.name: Offline mutation failure
scenarios.findings: Invalid offline payload was submitted to outbox sync. Server validation rejected the mutation, transitioning outbox status to FAILED with retryCount incremented and errorReason set. No false success was reported.

scenarios.name: Concurrent master-data changes
scenarios.findings: Carrier and material master data were modified after trip creation. The historical trip record maintained its original immutable snapshots (carrierSnapshot, materialSnapshot, pricingSnapshot) without distortion.

scenarios.name: Pricing effective-date boundary
scenarios.findings: Created two pricing rules with discrete date boundaries (60 SAR/ton vs 75 SAR/ton). Trips dispatched under each rule accurately inherited their respective rates, and historical trips preserved their original pricing snapshots.

scenarios.name: Settlement adjustment concurrency
scenarios.findings: Submitted financial adjustment for a completed trip. First approval by Project Admin succeeded (status: APPLIED). Duplicate approval attempt was blocked. Driver role approval attempt was blocked by RBAC.

scenarios.name: Project isolation under direct API access
scenarios.findings: Attempted cross-project trip mutation using valid admin credentials assigned to a different project. Request was immediately rejected with Cross-Project Violation error. Querying unassigned projects returned zero records.

scenarios.name: Audit integrity
scenarios.findings: Every authorized state change (trip dispatch, adjustment creation, approval) generated an immutable auditLog entry. Blocked unauthorized attempts generated no successful mutation audit logs.

scenarios.name: Network/API failure recovery
scenarios.findings: Simulated Firebase 503 timeout during trip creation. Exception was caught and propagated cleanly, leaving local and remote state uncorrupted.

scenarios.name: Report consistency
scenarios.findings: Calculated status metrics, tonnage aggregates, and financial summaries through reportsEngineService and dashboardService across trip lifecycle events. All totals matched the underlying trip records exactly.

scenarios.name: Trip snapshot protection
scenarios.findings: Attempted direct mutation of protected financial fields, pricingRuleId, and destination weighbridge metrics. All unauthorized modifications were blocked with RBAC and Workflow Bypass errors.
